citation: Alexander AS, Nitz DA (2017). Spatially periodic activation patterns of retrosplenial cortex encode route sub-spaces and distance traveled. Curr Biol 27:1551-1560
environment_type: closed plus-shaped track with recurrent segments
environment_size: Closed plus-shaped track run clockwise, 12 equal segments; Fig. 1B labels one segment 55 cm, so a lap is about 660 cm (derived, nominal; rats cut the corners, Fig. 1B right); 1 cm edges, open view of the room; reward at the arrow point. A quarter (3 segments, 165 cm) is the smallest repeating shape
familiarity: trained; on average 14 uninterrupted laps per session
measure: Spearman correlation of odd vs even trial population vectors at all pairs of route positions (Fig. 1D); mean and median r by separation read here
normalization: Spearman (rank) correlation across cells; per-cell normalization of the vectors not stated (Fig. 1C left shows max-normalized profiles)
smoothing: Gaussian 7 cm SD on the rate profiles
simultaneous_or_pooled: pooled: one vector of all cells across rats and sessions
dist_r05_cm: about 60 to 63 (median r; the bar clips at its 0.5 end)
zero_cross_cm: not readable (values below about 0.48 to 0.50 are clipped)
floor: clipped at the bar minimum beyond about 85 cm
far_behaviour: Peak 0.81 to 0.82; r = 0.7 at about 35 cm and 0.6 at about 48 to 50 cm; more than half the pixels reach the clipped floor at 60 to 63 cm and almost all by 85 cm; no off-diagonal repeats
quote_or_reading: "Unlike matrices for the CA1 ensemble, off-diagonal correlations for RSC ensembles exhibited repeating patterns across the track" (p. 1552); "Correlation matrices were computed using Spearman's correlations" (p. e4). Fig. 1 raster 1339 x 1617 px (xref 64) extracted from the PDF; matrices 512 x 512 px; Spearman bar in the raster with tick labels 1 and 0.5; each pixel mapped to the nearest bar colour, black turn lines and the white peak line masked; r averaged by |row - column| in 4 cm steps; 660 cm per matrix side; script kernel_an17.py. Two calibrations: bar ends = 1 and 0.5, or tick-label centres = 1 and 0.5 (bar then spans 0.48 to 1.03); values below give both where they differ.
notes: About twice as wide at r = 0.5 as the other rat CA1 curves (24 to 45 cm), possibly from the rank measure on pooled vectors with many silent cells and the 7 cm smoothing (inference). Distances assume 55 cm segments; corner cutting makes the true path shorter, so cm values may be up to about 10% high.
